findings.title: Invalid ERB conditional prevents rendering existing discussions
findings.body: The conditional ends with `end if`, but the trailing `if` has no condition. ERB generates invalid Ruby for this template, so requests for an embed whose topic already exists fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. Close the conditional with just `end`.

findings.title: Imported feed HTML bypasses sanitization
findings.body: Feed content is passed through Nokogiri fragment parsing and stored as a raw-HTML post, whose cooking method returns the input unchanged. Fragment parsing does not remove scripts, event-handler attributes, or dangerous link schemes. Consequently, active HTML supplied by a feed executes on the forum's origin when the post is rendered, including through the embed template's `raw post.cooked`. Sanitize the imported HTML before storing/rendering it, and escape the URL interpolated into the attribution link.

findings.title: Feeds without a content field abort polling
findings.body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Ordinary RSS feeds commonly provide article text in `description` or `content:encoded` rather than `content`, and Atom feeds can provide only a summary. A missing content value therefore raises instead of importing the entry, aborting the entire poll and preventing subsequent entries from being processed. Select the supported content fields with a fallback and handle entries with no body.

findings.title: Remote retrieval follows redirects outside the allowed host
findings.body: TopicRetriever validates only the host of the initial embed URL, then this `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without checking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including a private-network address, therefore causes the background worker to fetch that destination and potentially publish its contents as a topic. Validate the scheme and destination address for every request and redirect rather than relying solely on the original URL's host.

findings.title: URL absolutization mishandles relative and protocol-relative links
findings.body: The converter only handles values beginning with `/` and treats all of them as paths on the article's host. Thus `images/photo.jpg` remains relative and loads from the forum rather than the source article, while `//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg` becomes a path such as `http://source.example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg`. The same problem affects anchor links. Resolve references against the full source URL with URI-aware joining so imported images and links retain their intended destinations.
